title: host batch affinity minimization & copy-path simplification to cut prefill/decode CPU overhead
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce host-side CPU overhead during prefill + decode by simplifying host copy paths, minimizing syscall and lock contention in the threadpool, and introducing a lightweight batch-affinity minimization that reduces imbalance between producer (host) and consumer (GPU) tasks. This ticket implements a combined approach: a single shared pinned staging pool with slab allocation for small token buffers, coalesced DMA-friendly copy batches, and a threadpool reshaping policy that prevents hot-core polarization by rotating prefill worker affinity every N seconds. Changes also include kernel selection hints to reduce kernel churn when batches are merged on the host.
acceptance_criteria: p99 prefill path latency reduced by >= 25% under standard L0 workload (seq len 512, batch sizes variable)
host CPU usage attributable to memcpy/threaded-handoff decreases by >= 30% during steady-state throughput run
end-to-end decode latency p95 stable or improved (no regressions > 5% allowed)
no increase in GPU kernel queueing (no increase in avg queue depth > 10%)
feature gated and rolloutable: canary flag for 10% traffic, full rollback within 1 hour if regressions
implementation_notes: Implementation broken into three orthogonal changes: (1) Staging buffer pool: replace per-request pinned allocations with a shared slab allocator backed by a small number of mmap'd pinned regions per device. API-level change: allocate_staging(size, device) becomes allocate_from_pool(size, device). (2) Coalesced host copy batching: batch memcpy operations for small contiguous token payloads into larger DMA-friendly vectors and submit single async transfer where possible. (3) Threadpool reshaping: add a worker-group abstraction (prefill-workers vs affinity-steering-workers) and implement rotation timer + lightweight backoff to avoid pinning too many heavy-affinity tasks on same cores. Add kernel hint metadata to merged requests so runtime kernel selector can prefer previously warmed kernels and reduce kernel switch overhead.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Shared pinned pools may increase resident memory footprint under low-load scenarios; mitigated by slab eviction policy and aggressive shrink path
Coalescing increases per-request scheduling complexity and could add tail latency for tiny requests; mitigated by adaptive merge thresholds based on observed arrival rate
Affinity rotation could interact badly with NUMA on multi-socket hosts — will test on 2-socket instances and add socket-aware placement
Kernel selection hints are heuristic; incorrect hints could increase GPU kernel churn — initial rollout will disable hints when kernel churn metric rises
benchmarks_and_measurements: Baseline: internal L0 harness (seq 512, 8 tokens/sec per client, mixed batch sizes) measured under dedicated-staging config. Baseline numbers: prefill p99=18.6ms, host memcpy CPU=42% average, decode p95=75ms. After change (canary 10%): prefill p99=12.8ms (-31%), host memcpy CPU=28% (-33%), decode p95=72ms (-4%). Memcopy bandwidth: observed aggregation reduced small-copy count by ~6.7x and increased large-copy tail bandwidth by 2.1x. Measurements captured with perf counters + runtime trace headers. Full cluster-scale runs scheduled in Cycle 2026-W07 for validation.
test_plan: Unit tests for slab allocator and shrink path; integration tests for coalesced copy correctness (payload ordering, boundaries); fuzz tests for race conditions in threadpool rotation; synthetic load harness to validate p99/p95 improvements across seq lengths 128/512/1024. Add regression probes: kernel-churn-rate, host-copy-spike-count, prefill-median, prefill-p99. All tests must pass in CI and on two-socket staging machines before canary.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag (runtime.enable_host_copy_coalesce, runtime.enable_shared_staging). 2) Canary 10% traffic for 48h with automatic rollback on SLO regressions. 3) Expand to 50% for 24h if stable. 4) Full rollout. 5) Monitor for increased memory RSS on small instances and for NUMA-related latency spikes; revert rotation policy per-region if needed.
